title: BACKND Base common error handling patterns
summary: Operational error-handling patterns for recurring runtime situations: device block (403), bad/expired accessToken (401) and token reissue, maintenance, rate limiting (429), Unity main-thread handling, and other-device login detection. Complements the all-errors catalog with how-to-respond guidance and handler registration.
capabilities: map a recurring error situation to a recommended handling flow
explain token reissue (RefreshTheBackendToken) and re-login on bad accessToken
describe handler registration for maintenance, rate limit, and other-device login
distinguish this how-to-handle topic from the all-errors code catalog
prerequisites: A concrete error situation or status code is observed
Login/token context exists when handling auth-related errors
common_pitfalls: Treating bad accessToken as fatal instead of reissuing the token or re-logging in
Not registering the relevant handler before the error situation occurs
Calling Unity APIs off the main thread inside a callback
verification_required_for: exact error wording and status/error codes
current handler names and registration API
verification_strategy: Use https://docs.backnd.com plus the source route and cross-check live payloads before quoting exact error text.
Confirm handler and token-reissue method names from the official page before generating code.
public_notes: This topic is about how to respond to errors; all-errors is the code catalog.
Handler and token APIs are mutable; verify before generating production handlers.
